findings.title: Keyboard users land on a hidden, ring-less ⋯ button after leaving edit mode
findings.body:
Closing the edit composer now hands focus back with `focus({ focusVisible: false })`. In the same change, `comments.css` reveals a card's actions only on `:hover` or `:has(:focus-visible)`, where it used to use `:focus-within`.

Trigger: a keyboard user opens Edit from the ⋯ menu, then saves or cancels with the keyboard. Focus goes to the ⋯ button, but `:focus-visible` does not match, so:
- the actions stay at `opacity: 0`;
- the focused element shows no focus ring;
- the byline time stays put instead of making way.

The user is left on an invisible control.

Fix: keep `focusVisible: false` only when the edit was entered with the pointer. For example, record in `editReturnFocus` whether the opener had `:focus-visible`, and restore with the same value. Alternatively, keep a `:focus-within` fallback for the case where the pointer is not involved.
